items.plain: We know light by its opposite and colours by their contrasts. God made pain and grief so that happiness could be known through them.
items.core_idea: Pain exists so joy can be known

items.plain: We and the world are made new every moment, though we never notice it. Life is like a stream, always renewed, even though it looks continuous.
items.core_idea: Life is renewed every moment, unnoticed

items.plain: If you can't swim or sail, don't throw yourself into the sea out of vanity. A real swimmer brings pearls up from the deep and wins gain from danger.
items.core_idea: Take risks only where you have skill

items.plain: I use my grief as a healing salve for my eyes, so they fill with pearls. Tears shed under God's correction are pearls, though people think they are only tears.
items.core_idea: Tears from God's chastening are precious

items.plain: Love's garden has no limits and bears more than joy and sorrow. The true lover rises above both and stays fresh whatever the season.
items.core_idea: True love rises above joy and sorrow

items.plain: Why do you run from our cries here on earth, God? Why do you pour more sorrow on hearts already sorrowful?
items.core_idea: A cry to God about sorrow

items.plain: Don't judge by how ordinary people fare, and don't be thrown by harshness or kindness. Mercy and severity, joy and sorrow all pass away; only God remains.
items.core_idea: Joy and sorrow pass; God remains

items.plain: One fault among a hundred good qualities is like one dry stick in a green garden.
items.core_idea: One flaw is small among many virtues

items.plain: Sober thinking clings to memory, and past and future hide God from us, so burn them both away. How long will you stay divided into segments, like a reed?
items.core_idea: Past and future veil God from us

items.plain: You want to repent for the past, but how will you repent for that repenting? One moment you love the lute's music, the next you embrace weeping.
items.core_idea: Regret for the past is another trap

items.plain: Love and tenderness belong to our humanity; passion and lust belong to our animal side.
items.core_idea: Love is human; lust is animal

items.plain: Gifts friends give each other are only signs, outward proof of the love hidden in their hearts.
items.core_idea: Gifts are signs of hidden love

items.plain: God says: nothing above or below, not earth, sky or highest heaven, can contain me, yet I am contained in the believer's heart. Look for me in such hearts.
items.core_idea: God dwells in the believer's heart

items.plain: Hold back from idle, wandering thoughts, for there are lions in that desert. Restraint is the best medicine, just as scratching only worsens an itch; practise it and your soul grows strong.
items.core_idea: Restraint from idle thoughts strengthens the soul

items.plain: Fruit appears only when the blossoms fall. Bread must be broken to feed, grapes crushed to make wine, and citrons pounded to heal the sick.
items.core_idea: Breaking down comes before fruit

items.plain: You need a friend; don't walk this road alone or go your own way through the desert.
items.core_idea: Don't travel the road alone

items.plain: If every rub offends you, how will you ever be polished into a mirror?
items.core_idea: Friction is what polishes us

items.plain: Whoever sees and admits their own faults is moving fast toward perfection. Whoever thinks they are already perfect makes no progress toward God; no sickness of the soul is worse.
items.core_idea: Admitting faults leads toward perfection

items.plain: If you want to go beyond mere names and words, free yourself from self at once. Scour off the rust with contrition, like polishing a steel mirror, and you will see your own pure, bright essence.
items.core_idea: Free yourself from self to see your essence

items.plain: Darkness brings sleep and quiet, yet the water of life is found in darkness, spirits are refreshed there, and silence is when heavenly voices speak. Opposites come from opposites; light was made out of darkness.
items.core_idea: Light is born out of darkness

items.plain: Before God's commands, bow your pride. Don't mock or scold even those who go astray.
items.core_idea: Humble yourself; don't scorn the lost

items.plain: Nothing is more bitter than being cut off from you, God, and without your shelter there is only confusion. Our goods rob our souls and our bodies tear at them; without relying on you, how can we live?
items.core_idea: Without God we are lost

items.plain: See how delicate the heart is: one speck of dust was enough to cloud its moonlight.
items.core_idea: The heart is easily clouded

items.plain: Patience, not haste, will get you what you want. Be patient; God knows what is best.
items.core_idea: Be patient; God knows best

items.plain: It takes time for blood to turn into milk. Until your good fortune is born like a new baby, the blood does not become sweet milk.
items.core_idea: Good things take time to ripen

items.plain: If greed clouded a mirror, it would lie as we humans do. If scales were greedy for money, would they ever weigh anything truly?
items.core_idea: Greed distorts honest judgement

items.plain: Give up loving outward forms, for love doesn't depend on a face; if it did, why turn from the form when life leaves it? Lover, think hard about what you really love.
items.core_idea: Love is for the soul, not the form

items.plain: Learn to tell true dawn from false, the wine from the cup, so that instead of many restless eyes, one eye opens through patience and steadiness. Then you will see true colours, and jewels instead of stones.
items.core_idea: Patience lets you see what is true

items.plain: Love makes bitter things sweet, copper into gold, pain into healing, thorns into roses, a prison into a garden and grief into joy. Without love, soft wax turns to hard iron.
items.core_idea: Love transforms everything it touches

items.plain: Even when harm comes to you, look carefully at the one who does it. Seeing how good and ill rise and fall opens a way from misfortune to happiness, since each state gives birth to its opposite.
items.core_idea: Each hardship turns into its opposite

items.plain: God says he looks not at words but at whether the heart is humble, since the heart is what matters. He wants a burning heart: light the flame of love and burn away fine phrases.
items.core_idea: God looks at the heart, not words

items.plain: Good people seek out pain to heal, and wherever there is pain or poverty, help goes there. Don't seek water; just show you are thirsty, and water will spring up around you.
items.core_idea: Show your need, and help comes

items.plain: If you can't reach the Ka'ba yourself, show your helplessness to God, for crying out is powerful. As a mother waits for her child's cry, God sends his love's milk when you call, so keep crying to him.
items.core_idea: Cry out to God in your need

items.plain: Pain is a treasure full of mercies: the fountain of life lies in darkness and cold, and spring hides inside autumn. Keep company with grief and seek life in your own death.
items.core_idea: Pain hides mercy and renewal

items.plain: Someone who believes everything is a fool, but someone who calls everything false is a scoundrel.
items.core_idea: Neither believe all nor doubt all

items.plain: I am master of my thoughts, not ruled by them, as a builder is master of the building. All creatures are slaves to thought, and that is why they are sad; I go into thought and leave it at will.
items.core_idea: Master your thoughts; don't be ruled by them

items.plain: Look past names to qualities, so the qualities can lead you to the essence. Sects quarrel over God's names; when they reach his essence, they find his peace.
items.core_idea: Look beyond God's names to his essence

items.plain: Angels don't walk on land and animals know nothing of the sea. You are an animal in body and an angel in soul, so you move on both earth and heaven.
items.core_idea: You are both animal and angel

items.plain: God says: your calling 'Allah' was my answer 'Here I am'; your pain and longing were my messengers. Your struggles were my pull that started your prayer; each 'O Lord' of yours holds many answers from me.
items.core_idea: Your prayer is already God's answer

fix.display_text:
That calling 'Allah' of thine was my 'Here am I,'
And that pain and longing and ardour of thine my messenger;
Thy struggles and strivings for assistance
Were my attractions, and originated thy prayer.
Thy fear and thy love are the covert of my mercy,
Each 'O Lord!' of thine contains many 'Here am I's.

items.plain: Pain is better than ruling the world, because it makes you call on God in secret. The cries of people without pain are dull and cold; the cries of the sorrowful come from burning hearts.
items.core_idea: Pain makes prayer heartfelt

items.plain: Brave friend, hold on to God, who is beyond the worlds above and below. He stays with you when you have no home, brings peace out of turmoil, and keeps his promise when you suffer.
items.core_idea: Hold on to God, who never leaves

fix.display_text:
O brave friend, grasp His skirt,
Who is removed alike from the world above and below;
Who neither, like Jesus, ascends to heaven,
Nor, like Korah, sinks into the earth;
Who will abide with thee in the house and abroad
When thou lackest house and home.
He will bring forth peace out of perturbations,
And when thou art afflicted will keep His promise.
fix.reason: Stray full stop and scan error 'afllicted'

items.plain: The sea is not its foam, yet we watch the foam and miss the sea, tossed like blind boats on a bright ocean. You see the water; see the Water moving it, the Spirit within your spirit.
items.core_idea: Look past the foam to the sea

items.plain: You are rooted like grass, your head shaken by every wind. Your foot won't be free until you pull it out of the mud; the way out is hard, but when God frees you, you can go your way.
items.core_idea: Pull yourself free from the mire

fix.display_text:
You are footbound like the grass in the ground,
And your head is shaken by the wind uncertainly.
Your foot stands not firmly till you move it,
Nay, till you pluck it not up from the mire.
When you pluck up your foot you escape from the mire,
The way to this salvation is very difficult.
When you obtain salvation at God's hands, O wanderer,
You are free from the mire, and go your way.

items.plain: Be silent so you can hear God speak words no tongue can say, and things no book or talk can express.
items.core_idea: In silence you hear God

items.plain: Don't stare at your own image, beautiful or ugly, or at your weakness and baseness. Look at the one you love and long for.
items.core_idea: Look at your love, not yourself

items.plain: Knowledge has two wings; opinion has only one and flies lopsided, rising and falling as it tries to reach home. Once it leaves opinion behind and sees true knowledge, it spreads both wings.
items.core_idea: Knowledge flies; opinion stumbles

items.plain: The heart is like a feather blown about by the wind, or water boiling in a kettle; its purposes change every moment with its circumstances. So why trust its plans, and why make vows you'll be ashamed to break?
items.core_idea: The heart's purposes are unreliable

items.plain: The strange thing isn't that birds fall into traps they can't see, but that they see the trap and still fly into it on their own wings.
items.core_idea: We walk into traps we can see

items.plain: Sensations and thoughts are like weeds covering pure water. Reason clears them aside, and the wise then see the clear water.
items.core_idea: Reason clears thoughts to reveal clarity

items.plain: A part cut off from its whole is useless, like a limb torn from the body. Until it is joined again, it is dead and a stranger to life.
items.core_idea: Cut off from the whole, we die

items.plain: Don't think my feet walked the earth, for a lover travels with the heart, which, drunk with love, knows nothing of roads or distance. Near and far belong to bodies; spirits travel another way.
items.core_idea: The heart travels beyond distance

items.plain: All prophets' praises flow into one stream because the One praised is One, so in this sense all religions are one. People always mean to praise the One; they err only in their ideas of him.
items.core_idea: All religions praise the same One

items.plain: Never despair of God's grace; hold on to him, for many hard situations later ease. Hope often follows hopelessness, as sunlight follows darkness.
items.core_idea: Hard times ease; hope follows despair

fix.display_text:
One must not despair of the grace of such a Benefactor,
One must cling to the stirrup-straps of God.
Ah! many are the conditions which at first are hard,
But, are afterwards relieved and lose their harshness.
Oftentimes hope succeeds to hopelessness,
Many times does sunlight succeed to darkness.

items.plain: You load a ship without knowing whether you'll drown or arrive; if you waited to know, you would never trade. A timid heart gains nothing, for only the lamp that catches fire gives light.
items.core_idea: Nothing is gained without risking uncertainty

items.plain: Let others pale at bad luck; smile like the rose at loss and gain, for it smiles even when torn, and what God's decree takes is gain. Sufism is finding joy in the heart when trouble strikes.
items.core_idea: Find joy in the heart amid distress

items.plain: It is said: don't mourn your cattle if a wolf has raided your flock, because that disaster may prevent a bigger one, and that loss may spare you a worse loss.
items.core_idea: A loss may spare a greater loss

items.plain: With you, my love, hell would be heaven and a prison a rose garden. Without you, lilies and roses would be like flames of fire.
items.core_idea: With the beloved, hell becomes heaven

items.plain: I died as matter and became a plant, as a plant and became an animal, as an animal and became human. Why fear death will make me less, when I'll rise an angel, then something beyond imagining?
items.core_idea: Each death raises us higher

items.plain: Pour water from a pitcher into a stream: it doesn't flee the stream but becomes it. Its separate self is lost, but its essence remains, and it is not made less.
items.core_idea: Merging into the whole loses nothing essential

items.plain: Every heart has a window to other hearts, so they are not shut off from each other like bodies. Two lamps may stand apart, yet their light joins in one ray.
items.core_idea: Hearts are joined like lamplight

fix.display_text:
Since in each heart there is a window to other hearts,
They are not separated and shut off like two bodies.
Thus, even though two lamp-dishes be not joined,
Yet their light is united in a single ray.

items.plain: When love sparks in one heart it is returned in the other, and if you love God, God loves you, for one hand can't clap alone. The thirsty seek water, and water seeks the drinker.
items.core_idea: Love is always returned

items.plain: Vegetables boiling in a pot leap up and ask why they are burned. The cook pushes them down: she boils them not from dislike but to give them flavour and make them part of life.
items.core_idea: Trials are meant to ripen us

items.plain: Nothing is absolutely bad; evil is relative, and every poison or cure helps one creature and hinders another. Venom is life to the snake and death to us; the sea is a garden to fish and fatal to land creatures.
items.core_idea: Evil is only relative

items.plain: Am I worth less than a lamb or a deer, to have no shepherd? No, I have a Guardian fit to rule, who knows every wind that blows on me, cold or mild, and is never unaware or absent.
items.core_idea: God watches over me always

items.plain: What you call a throne is a prison; you think you rule, but you are shut outside. You can't even master your own passions, so how can you govern good and evil?
items.core_idea: Who can't rule himself rules nothing

items.plain: As children of Adam we heard heaven's melodies in Paradise, and beneath our earthly veil we faintly remember them. That is why music feeds lovers: it reminds them of their first union with God.
items.core_idea: Music recalls our union with God

items.plain: When you have become your own fortune, you can never lose it. How could you lose yourself, when your true self is your treasure and your kingdom?
items.core_idea: Your true self is a treasure never lost

fix.display_text:
When, O spiritual one, thou hast become thy own fortune,
Then, being thyself thy fortune, thou wilt never lose it.
How, O fortunate one, canst thou ever lose thyself,
When thy real self is thy treasure and thy kingdom?
fix.reason: Full stop scanned for comma after 'How'

items.plain: People are like demons chained by love of money, dragged off to toil in shops and fields. The chain is made of their fears and worries; don't think they wear no chain.
items.core_idea: Greed and fear chain us to toil

items.plain: Seek help from God, not from anyone else. Look for water in the ocean, not in a dried-up channel.
items.core_idea: Seek help from God alone

items.plain: Don't be afraid to admit your ignorance and guilt, so the heavenly Teacher won't hold back his teaching. Saying 'I don't know; teach me' openly is better than false pride.
items.core_idea: Admit ignorance so you can learn

items.plain: How long will you hide behind 'I was compelled' and ignore your free will, blaming God for your sins as Iblis did? You took pleasure and pride in those sins; no one feels such pleasure in acting under compulsion.
items.core_idea: Don't blame God for your own choices

items.plain: Trade your cleverness for wonder. Cleverness is only opinion; bewilderment is real insight.
items.core_idea: Wonder sees more than cleverness

items.plain: Age is a matter of mature wisdom, son, not white hair and beard.
items.core_idea: Age is wisdom, not grey hair

fix.display_text:
Age consists in maturity of wisdom, O son,
Not in whiteness of the beard and hair.

items.plain: To someone who sees only surfaces, real and fake coins look alike: gold can be blackened with smoke, and copper gilded to fool the simple. We look at the heart, not the outside.
items.core_idea: Look at the heart, not the surface

items.plain: Don't grieve over what is past; once something is done, don't torment yourself about it.
items.core_idea: Don't grieve what's done

items.plain: Your real treasure is hidden under a false one, like butter hidden in milk. The false one is your passing body; the true one is your divine soul, long unseen and overlooked.
items.core_idea: The soul lies hidden in the body

items.plain: I see the world full of blessings, fresh springs always welling up, branches dancing and leaves clapping like singers. All this glory is a mirror seen through a veil; what would it be if the veil were lifted?
items.core_idea: The world's beauty veils a greater glory

items.plain: It's true our bodily senses are weak, but within us is a mighty power. The body is like flint and steel: plain, yet able to strike fire.
items.core_idea: A frail body holds great power

items.plain: When my spirit recognises yours, we remember that we share one origin and are one at heart.
items.core_idea: Kindred spirits remember their oneness

items.plain: Words bear witness by being true, and actions by keeping promises, and a false witness of either is rejected. Your words and actions must not contradict each other if they are to be trusted.
items.core_idea: Words and deeds must agree

items.plain: Don't you know how beautiful your own face is? Stop warring with yourself: it is your own foolish thoughts, like poisoned claws, that wound your quiet soul.
items.core_idea: Our own thoughts wound the soul

items.plain: God, you turn earth into gold and made the first human from earth; your work is transforming, mine is mistakes and forgetting. Turn my errors into knowledge, and make me, who am wholly base, gentle and meek.
items.core_idea: A prayer to be transformed by God

items.plain: You began as fire, earth or air, and had you stayed so you would never have become human. Through change God gave you a better existence, and he will give you thousands more, each better than the last.
items.core_idea: Change carries us to better existence

fix.display_text:
On the day that you entered upon existence,
You were first fire, or earth, or air.
If you had continued in that, your original state,
How could you have arrived at this dignity of humanity?
But through change your first existence remained not
In lieu thereof God gave you a better existence
In like manner He will give you thousands of existences,
One after another, the succeeding ones better than the former.

items.plain: Don't foolishly beg the spear for mercy; beg the King who holds it. Why cry to spear and sword when they are only captives in his hand?
items.core_idea: Appeal to God, not his instruments

items.plain: God, I turn to your free grace and not to my own deeds. I set my hope on it, because you gave me my existence first, unasked, so I firmly trust your grace.
items.core_idea: Trust God's grace, not your deeds

items.plain: When a preacher has no light or life himself, how can his words bear fruit? He tells others to walk straight while he sways like a reed in the wind; however eloquent, his preaching hides a wavering faith.
items.core_idea: Words without inner life bear no fruit

items.plain: Think well of true friends even when they are harsh with you, because suspicion cuts you off from hundreds of friends. If a loving friend treats you roughly to test you, it makes no sense to distrust them.
items.core_idea: Don't let suspicion cost you friends

items.plain: God told Job he had given a grain of patience to every hair on his head. So don't dwell on your own patience; look beyond it to the One who gives it.
items.core_idea: Patience is God's gift

items.plain: God, you are hidden in yourself but seen in your gifts. You are the water and we the millstone, the wind and we the dust, the spring and we the garden: the cause unseen, its effects visible to all.
items.core_idea: God is unseen but known by his gifts

items.plain: Prince, even a kingdom from east to west is as brief as lightning, and any kingdom that doesn't last forever is only a dream. How long will you cling to an illusion that grips you like an executioner?
items.core_idea: Passing power is only a dream

items.plain: The moon shines and the dogs howl; everyone acts according to their nature.
items.core_idea: Everyone acts according to their nature

items.plain: A person's wings are their aims, so look at what a lover aspires to, not the good and evil on him. A fine falcon hunting mice is worthless; an owl devoted to the king is a true falcon.
items.core_idea: Judge people by their aspirations

items.plain: God, my shifting resolves come from you, so by the same command mercifully free me from indecision. You are testing me, so help me, and give me one guiding principle, not ten.
items.core_idea: A prayer for steady resolve

items.plain: The whole world runs from its own will and self toward forgetting and intoxication. People turn to drink to escape self-awareness for a while, knowing that this existence of thought, memory and will is a trap and a hell.
items.core_idea: People drink to escape the self

items.plain: Bodies are like sealed jars, one holding the water of life and another deadly poison. Look at the contents and you are wise; look only at the jar and you are misled.
items.core_idea: Judge by what's inside, not the vessel

items.plain: God, you are as close as my own face, and such nearness is itself a veil. You are nearer to me than my neck vein, so how can I call to you as if you were far away?
items.core_idea: God is too near to be seen

items.plain: It may seem like midnight to you, but to me the dawn of a joyful morning seems near. To ordinary people the world looks dead, but to God every part of it is alive with feeling and love.
items.core_idea: Dawn is near; the world is alive

items.plain: No buyer is more generous than God: he takes your worthless goods and pays with light for your heart. For a few tears he gives a sweet divine spring, and for each sad sigh a place in heaven.
items.core_idea: God repays our griefs generously

items.plain: Cook your pot slowly and skilfully, for food boiled in a rush is ruined. God could have made the universe in a moment, yet took six days, and a baby takes nine months: God works by slow degrees.
items.core_idea: God works by slow degrees

items.plain: The Prophet said it well: whoever leaves this world doesn't grieve over dying, but over the opportunities they lost.
items.core_idea: The dying regret lost opportunities

items.plain: Any misfortune or trouble is better than being cut off from God and forgetting him, because troubles pass and that separation remains. Happy is the one who keeps a watchful heart before God.
items.core_idea: Troubles pass; distance from God remains

items.plain: God lowers and raises, and nothing comes to be without both: the seasons, day and night, health and sickness, peace and war. The world flies on these two wings, so every soul lives in hope and fear, trembling like leaves.
items.core_idea: Life moves through lows and highs

items.plain: God is nearer to you than your neck vein, yet you shoot the arrow of speculation far away. You have readied your bow, but the game is right beside you and you aim too far.
items.core_idea: God is near; you look too far

items.plain: Strip off your proud intellect so that grace can always pour down on you. Cleverness is the opposite of humility; give it up and keep company with simplicity.
items.core_idea: Humility receives grace; cleverness blocks it

items.plain: Justice is putting each thing in its proper place, and injustice is misplacing it. Nothing God made is useless or wholly good or bad, not even vengeance or mercy; each helps or harms according to its place.
items.core_idea: Justice is everything in its place

items.plain: How can one prisoner caught in a trap free another? Everyone in the world is a prisoner awaiting death, except one or two rare people whose bodies are in prison but whose souls are in heaven.
items.core_idea: A prisoner cannot free a prisoner

items.plain: Don't get drunk on cups of outward forms, or you'll end up worshipping idols; the wine is in the cups but doesn't come from them. Look to the Giver of the wine, which no cup can hold.
items.core_idea: Look past forms to their Giver

items.plain: The Truth is your real self, not your body; it is higher than 'you' and 'me' and has no limits. Don't tremble in your shell, pearl: you are the sugar, not the cane, so hold to your real self.
items.core_idea: Your real self is beyond the body

fix.display_text:
The Truth is yourself, but not your mere bodily self,
Your real self is higher than 'you' and 'me.'
This visible 'you' which you fancy to be yourself
Is limited in place, the real 'you' is not limited.
Why, O pearl, linger you trembling in your shell?
Esteem not yourself mere sugar-cane, but real sugar.
This outward 'you' is foreign to your real 'you;'
Cling to your real self, quit this dual self.

items.plain: A guide's shadow is better than directions to God, and contentment is better than a hundred fine dishes. A seeing eye is better than a hundred walking sticks; the eye can tell jewels from pebbles.
items.core_idea: A guide is better than directions

items.plain: When the devout wail and the angels plead for them, God says the delay is for their good. Their need draws them to him; if he removed it at once, they would wander off and be lost.
items.core_idea: Delayed answers draw us to God

items.plain: Parrots and nightingales are caged because of their sweet voices; ugly owls and crows never are. In the same way, the disappointments of the devout serve a wise purpose.
items.core_idea: The devout are tried for their worth

items.plain: One sore spot in a healthy body takes all our attention and spoils our comfort. Likewise, when all goes well but one trivial thing, that failure keeps bothering us while we hardly think of our successes.
items.core_idea: One failure eclipses many successes

items.plain: When we're free of pain, our wishes show us a mirage of happiness that doesn't exist. Chasing it brings real pain, and afterwards we look back with regret at the painless state we gambled away and can't get back.
items.core_idea: Chasing imagined happiness brings real pain

items.plain: The best the world offers is a life free from pain, quiet and bearable, so we limit our hopes to that. The safest way not to be very miserable is not to expect to be very happy.
items.core_idea: Expect little happiness to avoid misery

items.plain: If all worldly things slip from your grasp, don't grieve, for they are worthless; if you owned a world, don't rejoice. Since you are meant to pass to a better world, hurry on, for this one is worth nothing.
items.core_idea: Worldly things are worth nothing

items.plain: Joy is like gold in the mines: found only now and then, by chance and without rule, mostly in tiny grains and rarely in heaps.
items.core_idea: Joy comes rarely, in small grains

items.plain: To judge how happy someone is, ask what troubles them, not what pleases them; the more trivial the troubles, the happier they are. Only the well-off are irritated by trifles, since real misfortune makes them unnoticeable.
items.core_idea: Trivial troubles show a happy life

items.plain: Don't build happiness on needing many things, because such a broad foundation is the easiest to undermine by accident. Keeping your demands as low as possible relative to your means is the surest way to avoid great misfortune.
items.core_idea: Need little to be safely happy

items.plain: Life is like a journey where the view keeps changing, and so do our wishes; we often find something better than we sought, by another path. Instead of pleasure we gain experience and insight, a lasting blessing.
items.core_idea: We seek pleasure but gain wisdom

items.plain: Searching for gold, the alchemists found other things: gunpowder, china, medicines, natural laws. In a sense, we are all alchemists.
items.core_idea: Searching, we find something else of value

items.plain: While doing something great, we don't see it as great; we just do what seems right at the moment. Only looking back on our whole life do we see how some inspiration led us down the one right path.
items.core_idea: Life's pattern shows only in hindsight

items.plain: Frivolous people live too much in the present, anxious people too much in the future; few strike the balance. Those always chasing future happiness are like donkeys following hay tied in front of them, living provisionally until they die.
items.core_idea: Living for the future wastes life

items.plain: Only the present is real and our existence lies wholly in it, so we should welcome every bearable, pain-free hour. It is the height of folly to spoil it with regret for the past or worry about the future.
items.core_idea: Only the present is real; enjoy it

items.plain: Only evils certain to come on a known date have a right to trouble us, and there are very few; most are merely possible, and even certain ones come at uncertain times. Always preparing for both leaves no peace.
items.core_idea: Don't let possible evils steal your peace

items.plain: Today comes only once and never returns; tomorrow is another day that also comes only once. Each day is an irreplaceable part of life, yet we treat life as a general idea that loses nothing if one day is wasted.
items.core_idea: Each day is irreplaceable

items.plain: We'd enjoy the present more if, while well, we remembered how every pain-free hour looked like lost paradise when we were sick. Instead we waste happy hours in bad moods and long for them only when trouble comes.
items.core_idea: We notice good days only once lost

items.plain: A person can only be themselves when alone. If you don't love solitude, you won't love freedom, because only alone are you truly free.
items.core_idea: Only in solitude are we free

items.plain: No one is in perfect harmony with anyone but themselves, not even a friend or partner. Deep peace of mind, the greatest blessing after health, comes only in solitude, and for someone rich within it is the happiest life.
items.core_idea: Deep peace is found in solitude

items.plain: Just as people huddle together for warmth on cold days, you can warm your mind by contact with others. But someone with plenty of inner warmth doesn't need to.
items.core_idea: A rich inner life needs little company
items.extended_text: On cold days people manage to get some warmth by crowding together; and you can warm your mind in the same way--by bringing it into contact with others. But a man who has a great deal of intellectual warmth in himself will stand in no need of such resources.

items.plain: Becoming friends with solitude early is like striking a gold mine, but not everyone can do it.
items.core_idea: Befriending solitude is a rare treasure

items.plain: One hidden drawback of seclusion: just as staying indoors makes the body sensitive to every draught, long solitude makes our temper so sensitive that trivial words or looks upset us, things busy people never notice.
items.core_idea: Too much solitude makes us touchy

items.plain: If you need solitude but can't bear too much of it, take some into company: say less than you think, expect little, and care little for others' opinion. Society is like a fire; the wise warm themselves at a distance.
items.core_idea: Keep a wise distance from society

items.plain: Envy is natural but is a vice and a misery, so stifle it as an enemy of your happiness. As Seneca says, stop comparing and you'll enjoy what you have; when many seem better off, think of those worse off.
items.core_idea: Stop comparing to escape envy

items.plain: Think a plan over carefully, allowing for the unforeseen that can upset everything. But once you've decided and begun, let it run without reworrying; as Goethe put it, see well to your girths, then ride on boldly.
items.core_idea: Deliberate carefully, then act without second-guessing

items.plain: When a misfortune has already happened and can't be changed, don't let yourself think it might have gone otherwise or been avoided. Such thoughts only make your distress unbearable and turn you into your own tormentor.
items.core_idea: Don't torment yourself with what-ifs

items.plain: When we've made obvious mistakes, we shouldn't gloss over or excuse them. We should admit them, see them in their full size, and firmly resolve to avoid them in future.
items.core_idea: Face your mistakes squarely

items.plain: Once we give in to gloom, dark visions arise that don't easily fade, because they might just come true. We can't judge how likely they are, so possibility slides into probability and we hand ourselves over to torment.
items.core_idea: Gloom turns possibilities into torment

items.plain: Night makes everything look black, so thoughts before sleep or in sleepless hours are as distorted as dreams, and darkest about our own affairs. By morning these nightmares vanish: night is coloured, day is white.
items.core_idea: Night thoughts darken; morning clears them

items.plain: Each day is a small life: waking is a little birth, morning a little youth, and going to sleep a little death.
items.core_idea: Each day is a little life

items.plain: The smallest annoyance can swell into a monster when we brood over it and paint it in glaring colours. It's much better to take a calm, matter-of-fact view of what is unpleasant; that is the easiest way to bear it.
items.core_idea: Brooding magnifies small troubles

items.plain: Hold small things close to your eyes and they block out the world. Likewise, the nearest people and things, however unimportant, take more attention than they deserve and crowd out what matters, and we should resist this.
items.core_idea: Small near things crowd out what matters

items.plain: Instead of thinking 'if only that were mine', ask 'what if this were not mine?' Picture your possessions, health, friends and loved ones as lost, since we usually learn their value only after losing them.
items.core_idea: Value what you have before losing it

items.plain: We often try to escape present gloom by imagining future success, inventing many fanciful hopes. Each one holds an illusion, and disappointment is certain when hard facts shatter them.
items.core_idea: Fanciful hopes lead to disappointment

items.plain: It is comforting to look back on the great misfortunes that never happened.
items.core_idea: Most feared disasters never happen

items.plain: Our thoughts should be kept in little drawers, so we can open one without disturbing the rest.
items.core_idea: Keep worries in separate compartments

items.plain: We must limit our wishes, curb our desires and temper our anger, remembering we get only a tiny share of what's worth having and must suffer many ills. Bear and forbear, or no wealth or power will spare us misery.
items.core_idea: Bear and forbear, or be wretched

items.plain: People want to use their strength and see its effect, and they are most satisfied when they make something, whether a book or a basket. There is direct pleasure in watching work grow daily until it is finished.
items.core_idea: Making something brings deep satisfaction

items.plain: Struggling with difficulties comes as naturally to people as digging to a mole, and having every want met brings unbearable stagnation. Overcoming obstacles, in work or thought, is the full delight of existence.
items.core_idea: Struggle is the delight of life

items.plain: If thinking can't shake off an outside influence, counter it with an opposite one. Get over an insult by seeing people who think well of you, and ease the dread of danger by focusing on how to prevent it.
items.core_idea: Counter a bad influence with its opposite

items.plain: To toughen the body, work and exercise it hard while healthy and accustom it to hardship. But when illness strikes, do the opposite: nurse and rest the affected body, because what is sick and weak can't be hardened.
items.core_idea: Train when healthy; rest when ill

items.plain: Give the brain all the sleep it needs to recover, because sleep is to a person what winding is to a clock.
items.core_idea: Sleep restores us like winding a clock

items.plain: In life it helps to be able to do two things: look ahead and overlook. The first protects you from loss and harm; the second from quarrels.
items.core_idea: Look ahead, and overlook

items.plain: Learn patience with people by practising it on stubborn objects, seeing their opposition as fixed by their nature. Being angry at people is as foolish as being angry at a stone that rolls into your path.
items.core_idea: Don't rage at people's fixed nature

items.plain: Two people are hardly ever in exactly the same mood, since it depends on their circumstances, work, health and passing thoughts. These differences cause friction even between the most compatible people.
items.core_idea: Differing moods cause friction between friends

items.plain: When a false claim is accepted, don't despair or think that's the end of it. Over time it will be examined and discussed, and usually everyone comes to see what a clear mind saw at once.
items.core_idea: Truth wins out over time

items.plain: Seeing clearly amid general delusion is like having the only correct watch in a town of wrong clocks. You alone know the time, but it does you no good, since everyone goes by the clocks.
items.core_idea: Being right alone is of little use

items.plain: You won't lose a friend by refusing a loan, but very likely will by granting one. Likewise, being a little proud rarely alienates people, while being too kind and obliging often makes them arrogant until there is a break.
items.core_idea: Too much kindness can spoil friendships

items.plain: Be careful not to form a very high opinion of someone you've only just met, or you'll probably be disappointed, then ashamed of yourself, and perhaps even harmed.
items.core_idea: Don't judge new acquaintances too highly

items.plain: If someone shows annoying traits, ask whether they're worth putting up with those traits again, even worse. If so, let it pass, knowing it will recur; if not, break with them at once and for good.
items.core_idea: Decide if someone's worth their faults
items.extended_text: If any person with whom we are associated or have to do, exhibits unpleasant or annoying qualities, we have only to ask ourselves whether or not this person is of so much value to us that we can put up with frequent and repeated exhibitions of the same qualities in a somewhat aggravated form. In case of an affirmative answer to this question, there will not be much to be said, because talking is very little use. We must let the matter pass, with or without some notice; but we should nevertheless remember that we are thereby exposing ourselves to a repetition of the offence. If the answer is in the negative, we must break with our worthy friend at once and forever; or in the case of a servant, dismiss him.

items.plain: When you come across meanness or stupidity, in life or in books, don't let it upset you. Treat it as new knowledge about human nature, like a mineralogist finding a perfect specimen.
items.core_idea: Study human folly instead of resenting it
